title: 111 consecutive games, zero errors: Wilson breaks MLB shortstop record
dek: Jacob Wilson, 24, of the Oakland Athletics set an MLB record with 111 consecutive errorless games at shortstop, surpassing Mike Bordick's previous mark of 110 games in 2002. Wilson last made an error on July 6, 2025.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Jacob Wilson set an MLB record with 111 consecutive errorless games at shortstop, breaking Mike Bordick's 2002 mark of 110 games.
bottom_line: Wilson's streak remains ongoing, and the next play on any given night could end it. What to watch: whether the record extends further and how opposing batters adjust to the pressure of facing a shortstop with near-perfect positioning and footwork. If the streak holds through the rest of the season, the narrative will center on whether this defensive standard becomes the expectation at the position going forward.
body: Jacob Wilson, 24, of the Oakland Athletics set an MLB record with 111 consecutive errorless games at shortstop, per ESPN. The milestone surpassed the Baltimore Orioles' Mike Bordick, who went 110 games without an error in 2002.

Wilson last committed an error on July 6, 2025, in a game against San Francisco. The record came in a period when the Athletics beat the Boston Red Sox 4-3 at Fenway Park on Sunday, ending a 12-series losing streak. In that game, Wilson fielded five plays: two popups (one involving a collision with second baseman Jeff McNeil on an infield fly), two grounders, and the middleman on a 4-6-3 double play. One grounder was hit deep into the hole by Ceddanne Rafaela, and Wilson made a long throw to first.

Wilson's preparation is systematic. He takes grounders with teammates about two hours before games on days he plays shortstop, a routine he maintains regardless of schedule. "I do that every day that I'm playing short," Wilson told ESPN. "The DH days I try to stay off my feet as much as I can, but every day I'm playing short I'm taking ground balls no matter what."

That discipline traces to his father, Jack Wilson, a 12-year major leaguer who also played shortstop. "He's a very defensive-first guy for me growing up by teaching me defense first before the hitting side of things and making sure you're always prepared to play defense every day," Wilson said, per ESPN.

Starting pitcher J.T. Ginn of the Athletics credited Wilson's work ethic. "It's pretty amazing the way he prepares and works," Ginn said, per ESPN. "That stuff doesn't come by chance. He's a great worker. He's put a lot of time into his defense."
